evals.name: database-choice-adr
evals.prompt: We are choosing a primary database for a new event-ingestion service. The service needs to store user events that have relationships (sessions, page views, and conversions) and must support real-time analytics queries. We considered Postgres, MongoDB, and ScyllaDB. We picked Postgres because we need real joins and ACID transactions for event integrity; we accept heavier operational overhead. Write the ADR for this decision.

assertions.text: The ADR file path follows `docs/decisions/NNN-<slug>.md` format
The ADR includes Context, Options, Decision, Why, and Consequences sections
The Decision section includes a date
Options lists the real candidates (Postgres, MongoDB, ScyllaDB), not straw-man choices
The Why section names the tradeoff explicitly (e.g. joins/ACID vs operational overhead)
Consequences mention what the decision makes easy and what it makes hard

evals.name: reversible-library-skip-or-brief-adr
evals.prompt: We're replacing `moment` with `date-fns` in the frontend. All date handling is behind a thin wrapper module `src/lib/dates.ts` that we control. Should I write an ADR? If yes, write it. If no, explain why not.

assertions.text: The response correctly identifies this as a reversible, cleanly-abstracted dependency swap and either skips the ADR or writes only a very brief justification
If skipping, the explanation cites the thin wrapper / reversible interface; if writing, it does not over-engineer the ADR
The response mentions that hard-to-reverse choices (schema, auth, data store, language) would need an ADR
